items.description: Kenya needs to lower the cost of electricity, create a more stable tax environment and undertake other reforms to attract private-sector investment and create jobs, according to the World Bank.

items.title: Zimbabwe’s Payments to Former White Farmers Reach $508 Million
items.description: Zimbabwe said that compensation to White farmers for land seized 26 years ago has now reached $508 million, as the southern African nation seeks to restore access to international capital markets.

items.title: US Benchmark Yield Hits Highest Since 2002 as Bonds Sell Off
items.description: The US benchmark yield climbed to the highest since 2002 as rising oil prices drove a renewed selloff in global bonds.

items.title: UK Is First Big Economy to Pay 6% on Long Debt Since Euro Crisis
items.description: The UK’s long-term borrowing costs hit 6% for the first time in almost three decades, making it the first major economy to pay a rate that high since the euro crisis was raging in 2012.

items.title: European Stocks Drop as Bond Yields Spook Investors; Banks Lag
items.description: European stocks declined as regional bond yields climbed, denting the appeal of equities and fueling concerns about the economic impact of higher borrowing costs.

items.title: Turkey Wants Fund Investors to Give Back ‘Excessive’ Profits

items.title: Hedge Funds Boost Bets on Euro Weakness as French Risks Grow
items.description: Hedge funds are loading up on options that will profit if the euro weakens against the dollar as political and fiscal risks mount in France.

items.title: India Oil Refiners Shift Tactics, Hire Ships to Cross Hormuz
